summary: If a husband throws a get to his wife, it counts only if it lands in a place that belongs to her, like her house, her lap, or her basket.

chunks.en: Someone who throws a get to his wife while she is inside
chunks.st: In a case of one who throws a bill of divorce to his wife, and she is in

chunks.en: her house or inside her courtyard,
chunks.st: her house or in her courtyard at the time,

chunks.en: she is divorced.
chunks.st: then she is divorced
chunks.stMore: as though he placed the bill of divorce in her hand.

chunks.en: If he threw it to her inside his house
chunks.st: If he threw it to her in his house

chunks.en: or inside his courtyard,
chunks.st: or in his courtyard,

chunks.en: even if it lands right by her on the bed,
chunks.st: even if the bill of divorce is with her in the bed,
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz explains that the get is with her in the bed.

chunks.en: she is not divorced.
chunks.st: she is not divorced.

chunks.en: Into her lap or into her basket,
chunks.st: If he threw the bill of divorce into her lap, or into her basket [kaltah],

chunks.en: she is divorced.
chunks.st: she is divorced, even if she was in her husband’s house at the time.

summary: The husband must tell his wife that he is giving her a get. If he throws it to her in the street, it depends whether it lands closer to her or to him.

chunks.en: If he said to her,
chunks.st: If he said to his wife:

chunks.en: "Take this loan document,"
chunks.st: Take this promissory note,
chunks.stMore: and it was a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: or she found it behind him,
chunks.st: or she found it behind him
chunks.stMore: and he did not tell her what it was but

chunks.en: and she reads it, and it is her get,
chunks.st: she reads what is written in it and discovers that it is her bill of divorce,

chunks.en: it is not a get,
chunks.st: it is not a valid bill of divorce

chunks.en: until he says to her,
chunks.st: until he says to her:

chunks.en: "Here is your get."
chunks.st: This is your bill of divorce.

chunks.en: If he put it in her hand while she was sleeping,
chunks.st: If he gave it to her in her hand and she was sleeping,
chunks.stMore: and he then

chunks.en: she wakes up, reads it, and it is her get,
chunks.st: woke her, and when she reads what is written in it, she finds that it is her bill of divorce,

chunks.en: it is not a get,
chunks.st: it is not a valid bill of divorce

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהּ הֵא זֶה גִטֵּךְ.
chunks.en: until he says to her, "Here, this is your get."
chunks.st: until he says to her: This is your bill of divorce.

chunks.he: הָיְתָה עוֹמֶדֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וּזְרָקוֹ לָהּ,
chunks.en: If she was standing in a public place and he threw it to her,
chunks.st: If the woman was standing in the public domain and her husband took the bill of divorce and threw it to her,

chunks.en: if it was closer to her,
chunks.st: if it fell closer to her,

chunks.en: she is divorced. If closer to him,
chunks.st: she is divorced, and if it fell closer to him,

chunks.en: she is not divorced.
chunks.st: she is not divorced.

chunks.en: If it was right in the middle,
chunks.st: If it is equally balanced,

chunks.en: she is divorced and not divorced.
chunks.st: there is uncertainty as to whether she is divorced or whether she is not divorced.

summary: The same rules about throwing apply to kiddushin and to paying back a loan. The mishnah also teaches about throwing a get onto a roof or down from a roof.

chunks.en: And the same is true for kiddushin.
chunks.st: And the same halakhot apply with regard to betrothal.

words.note: The way a man and woman become married.

chunks.en: And the same is true for a loan.
chunks.st: And the same halakhot apply with regard to a debt.

chunks.en: If his lender said to him,
chunks.st: If his creditor said to him:

chunks.en: "Throw me what you owe me,"
chunks.st: Throw the payment for my debt to me,

chunks.en: and he threw it to him,
chunks.st: and he threw it to him

chunks.en: if it was closer to the lender,
chunks.st: and the money fell closer to the creditor,

chunks.en: the borrower is free.
chunks.st: the creditor acquired the payment.
chunks.stMore: The debtor is absolved of his obligation to pay even if the money did not reach the creditor’s hand, e.g., it was stolen or lost after it was thrown and before the creditor was able to take it.

chunks.en: If closer to the borrower,
chunks.st: If it fell closer to the debtor

chunks.en: the borrower still owes it.
chunks.st: and the money was lost, the debtor is still obligated to pay.

chunks.en: If it was right in the middle,
chunks.st: If it was equally balanced

chunks.en: the two of them split it.
chunks.st: and was lost, the two of them divide it, i.e., the debtor owes half of the amount.

chunks.en: If she was standing on top of
chunks.st: If a woman was standing on top of

chunks.en: the roof and he threw it to her,
chunks.st: the roof and her husband was standing below, and he threw a bill of divorce to her,

chunks.en: once it reached the air above the roof,
chunks.st: once the bill of divorce reaches the airspace of the roof,

chunks.en: she is divorced.
chunks.st: she is divorced.

chunks.he: הוּא מִלְמַעְלָה וְהִיא מִלְּמַטָּה וּזְרָקוֹ לָהּ,
chunks.en: If he was above and she was below and he threw it to her,
chunks.st: If he was above on the roof and she was below, and he threw it to her,

chunks.en: once it left the area of the roof,
chunks.st: once it leaves the area of the roof,

chunks.en: even if it got erased or burned,
chunks.st: even if the wording was erased or the document was burned before it fell to the ground,

chunks.en: she is divorced.
chunks.st: she is divorced.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether a man may use an "old get," one he wrote and then was alone with his wife before giving it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: פּוֹטֵר אָדָם אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְגֵט יָשָׁן.
chunks.en: a man may send away his wife with an old get.
chunks.st: A man may send, i.e., divorce, his wife with an outdated bill of divorce,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel forbid it.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel prohibit him from doing so.

chunks.en: And what is an old get?
chunks.st: And what is an outdated bill of divorce?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁנִּתְיַחֵד עִמָּהּ אַחַר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ לָהּ:
chunks.en: Any get where he was alone with her after he wrote it for her.
chunks.st: Any case where he was secluded with her after he wrote it for her and before he gave it to her.

summary: A get with a wrong date, place, or name is not good. If the woman married again with it, she must leave both men, and the mishnah lists many fines that come with this.

chunks.en: If he wrote the date by a kingdom that is not proper,
chunks.st: If he wrote the date on the bill of divorce using a calendrical system that counts years in the name of a kingdom that is not legitimate,

chunks.en: by the kingdom of Madai,
chunks.st: or he wrote the date in the name of the kingdom of Media,

chunks.en: by the kingdom of Yavan,
chunks.st: or in the name of the Greek Empire, after it ceased to exist,

chunks.en: from the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: or he wrote the date counting to the building of the Temple,

chunks.en: or from the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.explain: The Rabbis said a get must be dated the way the government did.
chunks.st: or counting to the destruction of the Temple,
chunks.stMore: in all these case, the bill of divorce is not valid. In the time of the mishna, the local government was particular that documents be dated with the official government date. Therefore, the Sages instituted that this must be done in bills of divorce as well. If one deviates from this practice, the rabbinic dictates of bills of divorce have been violated, and the bill of divorce is invalid.

chunks.en: if he was in the east and wrote "in the west,"
chunks.st: If he was in the east and he wrote the location in the bill of divorce as in the west,

chunks.en: or in the west and wrote "in the east,"
chunks.st: or if he was in the west and he wrote the location in the bill of divorce as in the east,
chunks.stMore: the bill of divorce is not valid.

chunks.en: and she married again, she must leave this husband and that one,
chunks.st: If he divorced her with this bill of divorce and she remarried, she must leave both this first husband and that second husband,

chunks.en: and she needs a get from this one and from that one.
chunks.st: and she needs a bill of divorce from this husband and that husband.

chunks.en: And she gets no kesubah, and no
chunks.st: And she does not receive payment of her marriage contract, and not

chunks.en: fruits, no food, and no worn clothes,
chunks.explain: These are things a wife usually gets from her husband.
chunks.st: the profits from her properties that her husband consumed, and she does not have a claim to receive sustenance, and she does not have a claim to worn clothes that belonged to her, but which her husband used.
chunks.stMore: She cannot demand these items,

chunks.he: לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
chunks.en: not from this one and not from that one.
chunks.st: not of this husband and not of that husband.

chunks.en: If she took from this one or that one,
chunks.st: If she took any of these items from this husband or from that husband,

chunks.en: she must give it back. And the child is a mamzer from either one.
chunks.st: she must return what was taken. And the child that was born from this husband or from that husband that was conceived after she married the second husband is a son born from an adulterous relationship [mamzer].

words.note: A child from a forbidden marriage.

chunks.en: And neither of them, if a Kohen, may become tamei for her,
chunks.st: And neither this husband nor that husband, if they are priests, is permitted to become ritually impure by her when she dies, which a husband may ordinarily do for his wife.

chunks.he: וְלֹא זֶה וָזֶה זַכָּאִין לֹא בִמְצִיאָתָהּ
chunks.en: and neither gets the things she finds,
chunks.st: And neither this husband nor that husband have the rights to objects she finds,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ וְלֹא בַהֲפָרַת נְדָרֶיהָ.
chunks.en: or her work, or cancelling her nedarim.
chunks.st: or to her earnings, or to the annulment of her vows.

chunks.en: If she was the daughter of a Yisrael,
chunks.st: If she was an Israelite woman,

chunks.en: she may no longer marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: then through these two marriages she becomes disqualified from marrying into the priesthood,
chunks.stMore: due to the prohibition against a priest marrying a zona.

chunks.en: The daughter of a Levi,
chunks.st: If she was the daughter of a Levite,

chunks.en: from eating maaser.
chunks.st: through these two marriages she becomes prohibited from partaking of the tithe that is given to Levites.

chunks.en: The daughter of a Kohen,
chunks.st: If she was the daughter of a priest,

chunks.en: from eating terumah.
chunks.st: she becomes prohibited from partaking of teruma, even after she returns to the house of her father the priest.

chunks.en: And the heirs of this one and the heirs
chunks.st: And the heirs of this husband and the heirs

chunks.en: of that one do not inherit her kesubah.
chunks.st: of that husband do not inherit the rights to collect payment of her marriage contract if she dies.

chunks.en: And if they died,
chunks.st: And if the husbands die,

chunks.en: the brother of this one and the brother of
chunks.st: the brother of this first husband and the brother of that

chunks.en: that one do chalitzah and not yibum.
chunks.st: second husband perform ḥalitza, since she was betrothed to the second one as well, and they do not consummate the levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: The mishna proceeds to teach an additional halakha concerning a bill of divorce written not in accordance with its halakhot:

chunks.en: If he changed his name or her name,
chunks.st: If he changed his name, i.e., he wrote a different name in the bill of divorce, or he changed her name,

chunks.en: the name of his city or the name of her city,
chunks.st: or if he changed the name of his city or the name of her city,

chunks.en: she must leave this one and that one,
chunks.st: and she remarried on the basis of this bill of divorce, then she must leave both this first husband and that second husband.

chunks.en: and all these ways apply to her.
chunks.st: And all of those above-mentioned ways of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier clause of the mishna apply to her in this case as well.

summary: In some cases a widow's co-wives do not need yibum. If it turns out the rule did not really apply, a co-wife who married someone else must leave him, with all the fines of the last mishnah.
stIntro: The mishna teaches another halakha associated with the previous halakhot:

chunks.en: All the forbidden relatives whose co-wives, they said, are allowed to marry,
chunks.explain: A brother may not do yibum with some relatives, so their co-wives are free too.
chunks.st: With regard to all of those cases in which they said that a man who died without children and left behind a widow who is, to the man’s brother, one of those with whom relations are forbidden, e.g., she is his wife’s sister, not only is there no levirate bond for her, but the rival wives of the brother who died are also permitted to marry without either levirate marriage or ḥalitza.
chunks.stMore: The mishna discusses another case:

chunks.en: if these co-wives went and married,
chunks.st: These rival wives went and married another man without ḥalitza,

chunks.en: and it was found that these women could never have children,
chunks.st: and these widows with whom relationships were forbidden were found to be sexually underdeveloped women incapable of bearing children [ailonit].
chunks.stMore: Therefore, it became clear, retroactively, that the marriage to the dead brother was never valid, and accordingly, the rival wives were never exempt from the obligation of levirate marriage due to their being the rival wives of a forbidden relationship. Consequently, the rival wives were forbidden to marry anyone else without ḥalitza, and the rival wives must

chunks.en: she must leave this one and that one,
chunks.st: leave both this man whom they remarried, and that yavam,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they cannot enter into levirate marriage with him.

chunks.en: and all these ways apply to her.
chunks.st: And all of those above-mentioned ways of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier clause of the mishna apply to her in this case as well.

summary: If a man did yibum with his brother's widow and her co-wife married someone else, and then they found the widow could never have children, the co-wife must leave.

chunks.he: הַכּוֹנֵס אֶת יְבִמְתּוֹ וְהָלְכָה צָרָתָהּ וְנִשֵּׂאת
chunks.en: Someone who married his brother's widow, and her co-wife went and married
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to one who marries his yevama, and her rival wife went and got married to another man,

words.note: His brother's widow, whom he marries through yibum.

chunks.en: someone else, and this one was found to be unable to have children,
chunks.st: and it was found that this yevama was a sexually underdeveloped woman,

chunks.en: she must leave this one and that one, and all
chunks.st: the rival wife must leave this man whom she remarried and that yavam,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she cannot enter into levirate marriage with him. Because the yevama was a sexually underdeveloped woman, the obligation of levirate marriage never applied to her, and her levirate marriage did not exempt her rival wife.

chunks.en: these ways apply to her.
chunks.st: And all of those aforementioned ways of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier clause of the mishna apply to her in this case as well.

summary: If a scribe mixed up a get and a receipt, and the couple never really divorced, the woman must leave her new husband. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about a get that was written but not used.
stIntro: The mishna now discusses another case:

chunks.he: כָּתַב סוֹפֵר גֵּט לָאִישׁ וְשׁוֹבֵר לָאִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: A scribe wrote a get for the man and a receipt for the woman,
chunks.st: A scribe wrote a bill of divorce for a man, so that the man could divorce his wife with it; and he wrote a receipt for the woman, for her to give to her husband upon receiving payment of her marriage contract, verifying that she received the payment.

chunks.he: וְטָעָה וְנָתַן גֵּט לָאִשָּׁה וְשׁוֹבֵר לָאִישׁ,
chunks.en: and he made a mistake and gave the get to the woman and the receipt to the man,
chunks.st: And the scribe erred and gave the bill of divorce to the woman and the receipt to the man, and

chunks.en: and they gave them to each other,
chunks.st: not knowing what was written in the documents that were in their possession, they gave what they received from the scribe to each other.
chunks.stMore: The woman gave her husband a bill of divorce and the husband gave his wife a receipt, and consequently, there was no divorce at all.

chunks.en: and after a while, the get
chunks.st: And after some time, the bill of divorce is

chunks.en: comes out from the man's hand,
chunks.st: in the possession of the man,

chunks.en: and the receipt from the woman's hand,
chunks.st: and the receipt is in the possession of the woman,
chunks.stMore: and they discover that the divorce never actually transpired.

chunks.en: she must leave this one and that one,
chunks.st: If the woman had remarried another man, she must leave this, the first husband, and that, the second husband.

chunks.en: and all these ways apply to her.
chunks.st: And all of those above-mentioned ways of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier clause of the mishna apply to her in this case as well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: if it came out right away,
chunks.st: If the bill of divorce is immediately [le’altar] in the husband’s possession,

chunks.en: it is not a get.
chunks.st: this is not a valid bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: since he clearly never gave it to her. But

chunks.en: If it came out after a while,
chunks.st: if it is in his possession after some time,

chunks.en: it is a get.
chunks.st: then this is a valid bill of divorce,

chunks.en: It is not in the power of the first husband
chunks.st: since it is not in the power of the first husband

chunks.en: to take away the right of the second.
chunks.st: to eliminate the right of the second husband.
chunks.stMore: The assumption is that the husband did in fact give her the bill of divorce in the correct manner, but at some point, he took it back from her.

chunks.en: If he wrote a get to divorce his wife and changed his mind,
chunks.st: If one wrote a bill of divorce to divorce his wife, and reconsidered and did not give it to her,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he made her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: Although merely writing the bill of divorce does not dissolve the marriage, by doing so he disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even if he gave it to her
chunks.st: Even if he gave the bill of divorce to her

chunks.en: with a condition, and the condition did not happen,
chunks.st: conditionally and the condition was not fulfilled,
chunks.stMore: and therefore the bill of divorce did not take effect,

chunks.en: he did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: he did not disqualify her from marrying into the priesthood. A woman is disqualified from marrying into the priesthood only if the divorce takes effect.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether a divorced woman who stayed at an inn with her former husband needs a second get. The mishnah also teaches about a get that is missing signatures.

chunks.he: הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְלָנָה עִמּוֹ בְּפֻנְדְּקִי,
chunks.en: Someone who divorces his wife, and she stayed overnight with him at an inn,
chunks.st: With regard to one who divorces his wife, and afterward she spent the night with him at an inn [befundaki],

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: she does not need a second get from him.
chunks.st: She does not require a second bill of divorce from him,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: she needs a second get from him.
chunks.st: She requires a second bill of divorce from him,
chunks.stMore: since they may have engaged in sexual intercourse at the inn and thereby betrothed her once again.

chunks.en: When? When she was divorced after being fully married.
chunks.st: When did they say this halakha? When she was divorced following the state of marriage.

chunks.en: And they agree that if she was divorced after only being engaged, she does not
chunks.st: Beit Hillel concede that when she was divorced following the state of betrothal, she does not

chunks.en: need a second get from him,
chunks.st: require a second bill of divorce from him,

chunks.en: because he is not close with her.
chunks.st: due to the fact that he is not accustomed to her.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, there is no concern that they engaged in sexual intercourse, even though they spent the night together at the inn.

chunks.en: If he married her with a "bald get,"
chunks.explain: A folded get that is missing some signatures.
chunks.st: If a woman was married by her second husband on the basis of receiving a bare bill of divorce, i.e., a folded and tied bill of divorce that is missing signatures,

chunks.en: she must leave this one and that one,
chunks.st: she must leave both this, the first husband, and that, the second husband.

chunks.en: and all these ways apply to her.
chunks.st: And all of those previously mentioned ways of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier mishna (79b) apply to her in this case as well.

summary: A "bald get" is a folded get with more folds than signatures. Ben Nannas and Rabbi Akiva argue about who may sign to complete it.

chunks.en: A bald get:
chunks.st: With regard to a bare bill of divorce;

chunks.en: anyone may sign to complete it,
chunks.st: anyone, even those who are disqualified from bearing witness, can complete it,
chunks.stMore: i.e., sign it in addition to the primary witnesses, so that it will not remain bare.

chunks.en: says Ben Nannas.
chunks.st: This is the statement of ben Nannas.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: only relatives may complete it
chunks.st: Not all who are disqualified from bearing witness can complete it. Rather, only relatives

chunks.en: who would be fit to be witnesses in another case.
chunks.st: who are fit to testify in another case.
chunks.stMore: Rabbi Akiva permits only the inclusion of witnesses who would ordinarily be valid witnesses, but who are invalid here because they are relatives of either the husband and wife or the other witnesses.

chunks.en: And what is a bald get?
chunks.st: And what is a bare bill of divorce?

chunks.en: Any get whose knots are more than its witnesses.
chunks.explain: Each fold was tied and should have a signature.
chunks.st: It is any bill of divorce where the number of its folds is more than the number of its witnesses.
chunks.stMore: In a folded and tied bill of divorce, the bill of divorce is folded and the folds are then tied. Instead of having two witnesses sign at the bottom of the document, witnesses would sign on each tied fold. A bare bill of divorce has more folds than signatures, i.e., some folds lack signatures.
